slice: T1: bounded spill progress and saturated call boundaries
observed: N03a's synthetic ABI can use the entire allocation pool for call arguments. pin_call currently pins those copies before a later stack argument. A reload for that stack argument then has no location, and repeated spilling of generated spill temporaries grows the retry body. The historical large reproducer will not be rerun.

scope.call_preparation: When the outgoing register pins exhaust a stack argument's candidate pool, schedule this call's existing stack-argument stores before its existing pinned copies. Preserve stack offsets, store order, copy order, call operands and indirect-result identity. No movement outside the compiler-generated preparation sequence. Nonsaturated preparations retain their exact order.
scope.progress: Never recursively spill the short-lived temporaries introduced by this allocation's spill rewrite. A retry must spill at least one previously unspilled pre-rewrite virtual value; otherwise return a bounded allocation refusal before generating more spill code. Keep the existing 64-retry ceiling. No arbitrary new instruction-count or memory limit, no silent invalid allocation and no relaxed verifier.
scope.invariants: No change to C/EvoIR/MIR instruction semantics, register pools, ABI layout, interpreter, proof registries or verifier. This is a fail-closed allocator implementation repair. Successful outputs still require independent allocation verification.
scope.excluded: Copy preferences/coalescing, global allocation, new spill placement heuristics, new options, default optimization flips, N07, timing experiments and semantic-domain expansion. Size improvements are not claimed for this repair.

engineering_reference.detail: RABasic tests isSpillable before recursively spilling and returns allocation failure for an unspillable interval. This motivates an explicit progress boundary, not a borrowed proof or a copied implementation.

red: Four or more scalar call arguments on a three-register synthetic pool whose ABI consumes all three registers; require finite allocation and independent verifier success.
The analogous saturated wide bank and mixed-bank stack slots; keep all values and ordered stack offsets.
An impossible constrained use occupying the whole bank must return an allocation refusal instead of repeatedly spilling reloads.
Test-local candidate-visit budgets abort before substantial growth in the old implementation; no unbounded or historical multi-GiB reproduction.
Existing pressure, full-width spill, fixed/tied/early-clobber and selected-edge tests remain green; nonsaturated boundary order is unchanged.

acceptance.focused: Bounded RED becomes finite success/refusal as specified; independent allocation verifier passes every admitted synthetic and AArch64 case. A removed reload or forged allocation remains rejected.
acceptance.native: Both existing 384-case native corpora execute and agree with object twins. Every OFF object matches the C2 OFF log hash; compare to hashes, not retired historical payloads.
acceptance.six_units: Two frozen A/B OFF measurement plans reuse the same six original TUs, checked/unchecked twins and original selected-TU harnesses; hashes equal C2 regression receipts. No expansion of source-bridge or opaque-input claims.
acceptance.stop: Any AArch64 output drift or new refusal must be investigated, not relabeled behavior-preserving. If the progress rule cannot preserve existing admitted cases, retain the bounded counterexample and record a separate disposition before widening scope.

resources.retention: Keep the small reproducer, logs, hashes, manifests and receipt. Remove successful intermediate objects after measurement and handle checks; do not retain full disassembly.

claim_ceiling: Bounded progress repair for the observed synthetic boundary failure, with unchanged frozen AArch64 outputs. Not coalescing/spill-size improvement, a complete allocator, a backend proof, default performance admission or closure of all N03c.
